merger_description:
Howard Springs Op Co Pty Ltd and Waymark Hotel Properties No 43 Pty Ltd as trustee for the Howard Springs Property Trust (the **Acquirers**), propose to acquire the land and business of the Howard Springs Tavern in Howard Springs, Northern Territory (the **Acquisition**).

Howard Springs Tavern is a commercial hotel business located at 280 Whitewood Road, Howard Springs, NT, which offers dining, gaming machines and liquor retailing, both in-store and via a drive-through bottle shop.

The Acquirers are part of the Waymark Hotels Group, which owns and operates hotels (pubs) that provide food & beverage (including alcohol), gaming machines, accommodation services, and takeaway liquor retailing (bottle shops). The Waymark Hotels Group currently operates pubs and bottle shops in regional Queensland and the Northern Territory.

determination_table_content.details:
Howard Springs Op Co Pty Ltd and Waymark Hotels Properties No
43 Pty Ltd (as trustee for the Howard Springs Property Trust) (the
Acquirers) applied for a notification waiver in respect of their
proposed acquisition of the land and business of the Howard
Springs Tavern in Howard Springs, Northern Territory (the Howard
Springs Tavern), as described in the transaction documents
provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The Acquirers are part of the Waymark Hotels Group (Waymark),
which owns and operates hotels (pubs) and takeaway liquor retailing
(bottle shops) in regional Queensland and the Northern Territory. The
Waymark Hotels Group is part of the Vinta Group, a private real
estate group.
The target, Howard Springs Tavern, is a commercial hotel business
in Howard Springs, Northern Territory (approximately 29km south-
east of Darwin), which offers dining, gaming machines and liquor
retailing, both in-store and via a drive-through bottle shop.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Waymark and Howard
Springs Tavern in the supply of on-premises and takeaway
packaged liquor, dining, gaming and accommodation
services in Howard Springs, Greater Darwin or the
surrounding local areas
b. there are alternative suppliers of on-premises and takeaway
packaged liquor, dining, gaming and accommodation
services in Howard Springs, Greater Darwin or the
surrounding local areas.
• In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
